limitations: Self-serve units/prices are public, while taxes and enterprise terms remain unspecified. Website cancellation language and the posted order form differ; exact contractual notice obligations need confirmation for the customer's agreement.

sources.title: Boxes.dev product and plans
sources.locator: Manage your agents; Pricing; For Teams
sources.finding: The service runs native Claude Code and Codex on cloud computers with desktop, mobile, browser and CLI access. Teams pricing advertises SSO/SAML/OIDC, SCIM, audit logs and custom infrastructure; implementation, contract scope and enablement are not established by the marketing list.

sources.title: How Boxes.dev works
sources.locator: Start a thread, get a machine; Continue from any device; Return later
sources.finding: Threads run on managed Linux devboxes, by default copied from a prepared template. Each devbox has its own files, services and ports; several threads may share one devbox. External databases can remain shared. Sleep preserves files and memory but pauses execution. Destroying a devbox deletes its files and archives its conversations.

sources.title: Tour the desktop app
sources.locator: Opening platform paragraph; Find your way around; tools and keyboard shortcuts
sources.finding: The desktop workbench is distributed for macOS and Linux. The main Mac build requires Apple Silicon and macOS 12 or later, with macOS 13 needed for the bundled PostgreSQL copy tools. Threads, folders, devbox groups, terminals, files, Git/Review and browser tools form its main workspace.

sources.title: Use Boxes.dev on your phone
sources.locator: Install and open a project; Start or continue a task; Review files and use a terminal
sources.finding: The iOS and Android apps open existing cloud projects. They can start and continue threads, answer questions and approvals, stop work, inspect files and diffs, batch code comments and use a terminal. The /m link is an app-install route, not proof of a mobile browser workbench. Initial environment preparation and some administration remain computer tasks.

sources.title: Install and use the CLI
sources.locator: Install and sign in; switchboard; native interfaces; Agent permissions
sources.finding: The product-owned dvb CLI is installable on macOS and Linux x64/arm64. It opens native agent interfaces, lists and reads threads, starts work, runs shell commands, manages machines, MCPs and permissions. Workstation sign-in is separate; managed machines use dvb-onbox instead. Claude input control transfers require confirmation.

sources.title: Connect Codex and Claude
sources.locator: Connect an account; Add a model provider; account switching and limits
sources.finding: Codex supports ChatGPT login, OpenAI keys, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway and compatible custom streaming Responses endpoints. Claude supports Claude login or API keys. Saved accounts can switch or rotate, with optional separately billed API fallback. Providers remain fixed within Codex threads; a new provider starts a new conversation.

sources.title: Models, reasoning, and usage
sources.locator: Model and effort pickers; provider restrictions; Inspect recorded activity
sources.finding: Model, reasoning and speed are configurable per thread within supported choices. Claude Ultracode workflows are harness functionality. Saved conversation activity includes tokens, calls and context charts, not reconciled dollar spend. Other activity is one combined series, missing history is identified and provider quotas are separate from machine box-hours.

sources.title: Choose project setup
sources.locator: Choose your starting point; Before you begin; Where setup starts
sources.finding: Users sign in and connect an agent, then use local-agent setup, the desktop local-folder wizard, a Team Template, or GitHub setup for subsequent projects. GitHub login is optional for local setup. Machine size is chosen at creation, applies across the project and is not resizable in place; each size includes 100 GB disk.

sources.title: Local folder setup
sources.locator: Review the setup scans; Check the final bundle; Fine-tune what gets copied
sources.finding: Read-only local scans prepare an upload bundle. The user selects repositories, local edits, untracked files, config, databases and optional history before upload. SSH, GitHub credentials and signing choices are explicit. Remote agents prepare the template; snapshots initialize later work.

sources.title: Agent command reference
sources.locator: Resource commands; thread start, read, send, interrupt, wait, artifacts and permissions
sources.finding: Scripting commands expose project, machine and thread inventory, creation, reading, follow-up, interruption and observation with explicit IDs and JSON. On-box tools have their own permissioned operations for agent delegation, messages, artifacts and settings. These IDs describe threads and devboxes, not a documented native issue database.

sources.title: Connect an outside assistant
sources.locator: Connect your assistant; Find or start a task; Stop current work
sources.finding: The remote MCP endpoint is https://api.boxes.dev/mcp. OAuth grants selected projects and read, task-control, event or settings scopes. It can inspect, start and follow up on the owner's threads and interrupt current work. Teammates' shared threads and approval dialogs are excluded; stops preserve queued work and event subscriptions need renewal within 24 hours.

sources.title: Add MCP servers
sources.locator: Add and authorize a server; project and agent scope
sources.finding: Boxes.dev manages MCP connections for Codex and Claude, including separate OAuth sign-ins and project scope. An MCP client connection adds external tools to agents and is separate from the remote MCP service that exposes Boxes.dev to outside assistants.

sources.title: Install agent plugins
sources.locator: Destinations; managed plugins; Update or remove
sources.finding: Plugins install skills and tools for Codex or Claude. Supported verified public GitHub plugins can be managed at a pinned commit across a project. Local/private/per-machine plugins stay template-local. ChatGPT account plugins and inherited harness sign-ins have different scopes.

sources.title: Agent settings
sources.locator: Project JSON/TOML; synchronization; validation; team inheritance
sources.finding: Claude JSON and Codex TOML settings synchronize to project machines. Running boxes update within a minute; sleeping boxes on wake. Some settings require a new session. Repository settings take precedence. Concurrent saves require loading the latest values; plugins and MCPs have separate management pages.

sources.title: Give useful instructions
sources.locator: Ask for checks; Save instructions for future work
sources.finding: Repository AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md retain versioned guidance. Project Agent guidance is applied to newly prepared devboxes, with Team Template guidance first in managed projects; changing it does not update existing sessions. Verification and delivery boundaries are prompt instructions, not proof of enforced gates.

sources.title: Keep an agent working toward a goal
sources.locator: Set a useful goal; Follow progress; Review before finishing; Claude goals
sources.finding: A saved goal keeps an agent working across responses. Codex goals can be edited, paused or resumed in the same thread and expose blocked and budget-limited states. Claude goals have different controls and a 4,000-character condition limit. Goal achieved still requires human review; it is not an independent acceptance gate.

sources.title: Shared project storage
sources.locator: Share Claude project memory; Understand persistence; consistency cautions
sources.finding: The open-beta /project share outlives devboxes but is deleted with the project. Claude automatic project memory uses /project/.claude/memory unless its settings override that. Codex can use ordinary shared files but its state/transcripts are not moved. Writes can conflict, and the share does not provide strict consistency or multi-writer file locks.

sources.title: Organize and share threads
sources.locator: Grouping; search; sharing restrictions; Copy transcript; subagent conversations
sources.finding: Threads can be named, pinned, archived, restored and searched across titles, prompts and final replies, including archives. Agent-created devboxes group under their creator. Sharing is read-only: teammates cannot prompt, approve, stop, open a terminal or control the machine. Copy transcript produces Markdown; media/history access has distinct persistence rules.

sources.title: Agent permissions
sources.locator: Create and read threads; Message other agents; temporary grants; Claude modes
sources.finding: Users can let agents create devboxes, read threads, message agents and pause/resume their own workers with scoped permissions. Both ends need messaging permission. Settings/template grants last three hours; certain integration actions require separate exact approval. Claude defaults to Full-access unless a custom policy applies, with Auto, Manual and Plan modes subject to model and machine support.

sources.title: Schedules and run history
sources.locator: Capacity and overlap behavior; run states; cleanup; Slack output
sources.finding: Vendor schedules support recurrence and timezone, optional idle-machine sleep and bounded capacity retries. Overlapping manual/scheduled launches can skip. API, Slack and Linear events are independent. Run ready means launch success, not task completion. History retains launch settings and archived conversations; cleanup deletes machine files and has explicit safeguards.

sources.title: Create an automation
sources.locator: Create, pause, activate, Run now and agent editing
sources.finding: Automations store prompt, agent and model settings and can be manual, scheduled, API, Slack or Linear driven. New automations begin paused and can be tested with Run now. Agents need approved temporary automation-editing permission to create or change them.

sources.title: Trigger an automation through the API
sources.locator: Idempotency; configurable input; existing targets; accepted run; status endpoint
sources.finding: An activated automation exposes secret-authenticated POST run/wake operations and GET launch status. Configurable requests select prompt, model and targets; identical idempotency keys replay the original run while changed input conflicts. Existing-devbox threads share files, not conversation. Status reports launch/delivery, not final output; use the thread for results.

sources.title: Work from Slack
sources.locator: Team connection; linked account; start and continue requests
sources.finding: A team admin connects Slack and each member links an account/automation. Mentions and thread replies route work to the linked owner's cloud environment and return updates. Slack context and attachments reach the agent; this integration does not establish native issue management or unrestricted shared prompting.

sources.title: Work from Linear
sources.locator: Start and follow a task; Send a follow-up; Attach work products
sources.finding: Linear Agent Sessions provide issue context and stable external issue identifiers. Progress and final answers return to Linear and result URLs can be attached. Repeated session events reuse a thread. Only the linked Linear account can follow up or stop; other people's replies are refused. Linear remains the issue tracker.

sources.title: Start and continue a thread
sources.locator: Queue versus Steer; Stop; drafts; attachments; import
sources.finding: Codex and Claude support queued follow-ups and steering with different interruption semantics. Stopping a response can leave queued work able to run. Drafts and failed-start recovery retain requests; attachments include files, folders and model-dependent images. Reusing a devbox shares its files, while changing Codex provider needs a new thread.

sources.title: Notifications
sources.locator: Attention markers; desktop defaults; quiet hours; mobile push
sources.finding: Completion, failures and input requests can notify on desktop/mobile, link to the thread and maintain unread markers across devices. Quiet hours and pause suppress alerts but preserve pending questions. Desktop defaults notify when unfocused; sound defaults on. Muting completion does not mute input requests.

sources.title: Sleep, wake, and recover a devbox
sources.locator: Automatic sleep; timed checks; Reset; Reboot; recovery notice
sources.finding: Default inactivity sleep is about five minutes, configurable to 15/30/60. Active agents and bounded background protection can keep a box awake. Sleep saves memory/files but pauses work. Reset kills processes and retains files; reboot loses in-memory state. Recovery notices identify restored memory/files and snapshot time. There is no documented guaranteed lossless failover.

sources.title: Startup, teardown, and maintenance
sources.locator: Startup; teardown; template maintenance and GitHub watches
sources.finding: Project startup, teardown and template-maintenance scripts prepare and maintain environments. Template snapshots and managed Team Template versions feed future devboxes. Lifecycle commands are environment automation rather than enforced product-spec or test acceptance.

sources.title: Environment files and secrets
sources.locator: Environment files; member overrides; propagation
sources.finding: Boxes.dev supplies configured environment files and variables to project machines with team/member scopes. Delivered values are readable by software and agents with machine access; changing or removing a managed value does not revoke credentials or erase unrelated copies.

sources.title: Team access and roles
sources.locator: Members/Admins; remove member; shared environments; static egress
sources.finding: Admin and Member roles have distinct template, membership, integration and billing privileges. Each member owns projects/devboxes and personal credentials. Shared workbench access is read-only. Removal offers transfer/keep/delete workflows, stops running work and pauses automations. Static egress requires enablement and is limited to configured public TCP destinations.

sources.title: Transfer a thread to a teammate
sources.locator: Before transfer; How your work moves; failure handling
sources.finding: An idle Codex/Claude thread can transfer to a teammate with a matching template or repository. History and packaged Git changes move to a new devbox using recipient credentials. Existing environment files are excluded; missing extra data depends on agent packaging. The source is archived after success; live processes are not transferred.

sources.title: Browse, edit, and transfer files
sources.locator: Workspace search; previews; uploads/downloads; conflict handling
sources.finding: Files searches filenames/text and edits current machine files with save/conflict indicators. It previews Markdown, images, videos, PDFs and HTML via Browser. Desktop transfers allow files up to 5 GiB; phone downloads allow 100 MB. Folder download requires an archive. Machine-local files are lost when the devbox is destroyed.

sources.title: Review code and leave comments
sources.locator: Comment on file/diff; Review and send the batch; Check the revision
sources.finding: Line and range comments from Files or Git/Review collect into one Code review attachment for the agent, including phone comments. These are not GitHub PR comments. File/range/PR references preserve context, but line contents can change; reviewers must check the revision. This is feedback, not a durable exact-revision approval gate.

sources.title: Commit, push, and open a pull request
sources.locator: Review/commit; PR creation; merge; automated follow-ups; attribution
sources.finding: Git/Review stages hunks, commits, reverts edits, creates/pushes branches and GitHub PRs and displays checks/conflicts. Pull-and-push supports rebase/merge. Optional PR follow-ups respond to checks, human/bot feedback and conflicts with documented batching and pause rules. Merged-PR notices indicate landing; optional commit trailers link threads.

sources.title: Review branch history and add repositories
sources.locator: Branch history; repository selector; branch operations
sources.finding: The workbench lists repository history, branch and commit ranges and repositories within a project. Branch operations are separate from devbox filesystem isolation. Git history is the revision record; the product does not establish arbitrary native issue dependencies.

sources.title: Share a running app
sources.locator: Public links; stopping sharing
sources.finding: A devbox port can be exposed by a public preview link. Anyone with the URL can use it until sharing stops. Revocation blocks new requests and closes public WebSockets within 30 seconds but cannot erase downloaded responses or close unrelated access paths.

sources.title: Plans, seats, and box-hours
sources.locator: Self-serve plans; trial rules; capacity; larger machines; Team Template billing
sources.finding: Trial grants 20 box-hours per user. Starter is USD 19/seat/month with 50 hours, Pro USD 99 with 300, Max USD 249 with 750. Per-user awake-devbox caps are 3/5/12/25 plus the template; projects 2/5/10/20. Standard compute is 4 vCPU/8 GiB. Paid overage uses shared prepaid credits at USD 0.40/box-hour before volume discounts. Template awake time counts; sleeping time does not.

sources.title: Manage billing and usage
sources.locator: Hourly history; seat and cancellation rules; credit limits; mobile devices
sources.finding: Usage history shows the owner's compute by hour/day and per-box contribution, updating on completed hourly windows. Paid seats have individual included hours; overage credits pool by team. Credits require a paid plan and purchases start at USD 20 with a USD 1,000/team/month cap. Optional auto-reload has a separate cap. Cloud mobile devices/builders use separate credit charges. Cancellation takes effect at period end.

sources.title: Your data and credentials
sources.locator: Copied files; credentials; machine sharing; stored history; deletion
sources.finding: Code and secrets selected for upload reside on cloud machines and are usable by their tools/agents. Selected SSH/signing private keys may be copied explicitly. Tokens/member files have scoped encrypted storage but authorized services and machine software can decrypt/read them. Saved history is also stored by Boxes.dev. Analytics, Sentry logs and masked replay are disclosed. Machine deletion archives threads; account deletion has billing and backup exceptions.

sources.title: Contact support
sources.locator: Feedback channels; CLI reports; diagnostics
sources.finding: Support is available through hi@boxes.dev, the public support page and in-app feedback. dvb report-bug includes description, CLI version/platform and account information, not repository files or environment variables automatically. Security reports go to security@boxes.dev. No general support response SLA is given.

sources.title: Boxes.dev changelog
sources.locator: November 19, 2026, Version 1.0.1135; November 17, Version 1.0.1134
sources.finding: Release 1.0.1135 is dated 2026-11-19 and adds HTML review, first-thread archiving and optional devbox/tab sidebar layout; PR follow-ups ignore late edits of bot status comments. The prior release adds Codex GPT-6.2-Sol/Astra and web Team Template setup. These are release dates, not retrieval dates.

sources.title: Boxes.dev privacy policy
sources.locator: Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10
sources.finding: The policy discloses account/device/session data, masked replay, Convex, Cloudflare, Expo, OpenAI title generation, Amplitude and Sentry. Replay retention is generally up to 30 days; other retention/backups lack fixed durations. International processing may occur in the US/other provider locations. Third-party agent terms are separate. No training promise is general to all customer content; narrower Google/Slack commitments must stay scoped.

sources.title: Boxes.dev terms of service
sources.locator: Cloud Service; Subscription Period; Non-Renewal Notice; data deletion and backups
sources.finding: Boxes, Inc. offers a cloud-service agreement with a one-month subscription period, tier/usage fees and incorporated Common Paper terms. The posted order form says 30 days' non-renewal notice, while the billing guide describes cancellation at the period end. Separate signed cover pages can replace these terms. This is not an open-source license grant.

sources.title: Boxes.dev for teams
sources.locator: Infrastructure options; Plans sized around your workflow
sources.finding: Custom pricing, hour pools and dedicated resources are available through discussion. The team brief says the vendor is open to hosting on customer infrastructure; it does not establish a downloadable self-hosted control plane.

sources.title: Security at Boxes.dev
sources.locator: Credential guidance; Vulnerability Disclosure Policy; What to expect
sources.finding: Security guidance and vulnerability reporting are public; the vendor commits to acknowledging vulnerability reports within three business days. This is not a support SLA, SOC 2 report or ISO certificate.

sources.title: Boxes.dev App Store listing
sources.locator: Compatibility; Version History; account prerequisite
sources.finding: The public iOS/iPadOS listing requires version 16.4 or later, distributes version 1.0.1135 and requires an existing Boxes.dev account. Its seller is ND Innovations LLC. Store download price alone does not establish free compute access.

sources.title: Boxes.dev Google Play listing
sources.locator: About this app; Updated on
sources.finding: The public Android listing is dated updated 2026-11-19 and offers thread history, follow-ups and notifications. Its description still calls account access early access/waitlist, unlike the current self-serve website/help. Successful signup and region-specific eligibility were not tested.

sources.title: Workstation CLI distribution 1.0.1135
sources.locator: package.json os/cpu/license/bin; tarball standalone-manifest.json and scripts/postinstall.mjs
sources.finding: The exact npm release is UNLICENSED, exports dvb/dvbd and distributes darwin/linux x64/arm64 archives with SHA-256 checks. The inspected shell wrapper executes the installed standalone runtime. Tarball SHA-256 d41fe950a7504c2019a999276e535a8d36b84b0aa8fbe735e0f4fa7ab61df844. No upstream Git commit is published.

sources.title: Published CLI runtime 1.0.1135
sources.locator: package/package.json; dist/bin/dvb.mjs lines 300360-302304; dist/product-docs/references/agent-tools.md and onbox-agent-tools.md
sources.finding: The readable released bundle implements thread start/control/read/observation command routing and ships agent-tool documentation. It is UNLICENSED and includes React/Ink CLI dependencies. Pin is npm version 1.0.1135, tarball SHA-256 213b030dae6a0fb83fd7861ab63ecc467f40a9ad16e7f2dd2613438af936fa18; no public upstream Git commit is exposed, so this distribution inspection is recorded as documented evidence rather than commit-pinned source-inspected. It cannot establish closed server enforcement or desktop/mobile implementation.

sources.title: Versioned product documentation in the CLI runtime
sources.locator: package/dist/product-docs/references/security-and-data.md, Desktop app logs, line 344
sources.finding: The versioned product documentation identifies the desktop main-process log as ~/.devbox/logs/desktop-electron-main.log. This supports an Electron desktop implementation, without access to its full build source or proof of mobile framework. Same package SHA-256 213b030dae6a0fb83fd7861ab63ecc467f40a9ad16e7f2dd2613438af936fa18; upstream Git commit unavailable.

sources.title: Slack teammate authorization and follow-ups
sources.locator: Follow up in the same Slack thread; Let teammates start work in your project; private-channel and owner authorization rules
sources.finding: Owners can authorize selected or any linked teammates to start work and send follow-ups in linked Slack threads, including tasks the owner started. Both people must be active on the same Boxes.dev team with linked Slack accounts. No one is the default and teammates cannot grant themselves access. Follow-ups target the same agent and identify their sender; active work receives Steer unless the owner chooses Queue. Work uses the owner's environment, credentials and usage. Private-channel restrictions also apply after launch.
